largestHolders.name: Novo Holdings A/S (wholly owned by the Novo Nordisk Foundation)

structure.note: A shares (1,074,872,000, unlisted, 100 votes each) are all held by Novo Holdings A/S, which is wholly owned by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and cannot divest them; B shares (3,390,128,000 issued, 10 votes each) are listed in Copenhagen and as ADRs on the NYSE. With its A shares plus B shares of nominally DKK 17,756,050, Novo Holdings held 28.1% of the capital and 77.3% of the votes at 31 December 2025. In practice A and B shares receive the same dividend per share.

notes: Fiscal year ended 31 December 2025. Sources are Novo Nordisk's Annual Report 2025, Remuneration Report 2025 and Form 20-F 2025 (PDFs on novonordisk.com). DKK, converted exactly from DKK million. LEADER: Lars Fruergaard Jørgensen stepped down as president and CEO on 6 August 2025 and was succeeded by Maziar Mike Doustdar on 7 August 2025. The Remuneration Report's table of executives' shareholdings at 31 December 2025 no longer includes him (it lists Doustdar, Karsten Munk Knudsen and non-registered executives), and the 20-F gives only the group total of board members and executives (1,173,813 B shares, 0.03% of the class). No holding is reported, so status is 'no-reported-stake'; this does not mean he holds no shares (he held 590,550 B shares at 31 December 2024). HOLDER: Novo Holdings A/S's 28.1% is of total share capital (A plus B), so it is economic; its 77.3% voting share comes from the A shares' 100 votes. The Novo Nordisk Foundation's interest is the same holding (it owns Novo Holdings 100%), so it is not listed separately. The 20-F lists no other holder above 5% of any class (as of 3 February 2026). DIVIDENDS: DKK 51,763 million paid to all shareholders including Novo Holdings. BUYBACKS: DKK 1,388 million purchase of treasury shares in 2025; a new programme of up to DKK 15 billion began on 4 February 2026, after the fiscal year. STOCK COMP: DKK 1,435 million total share-based payment expense (note 5.1). GEOGRAPHY: the five reported areas under the new 2025 structure (USA, plus International Operations split into EUCAN, Emerging Markets, APAC and Region China); comparatives were restated. Rounded segments sum to 309.07 against the stated 309.06.

paidout.notes: IFRS, Annual Report 2025 (fiscal year ended 31 December 2025). Interest received, interest paid and income taxes paid are all classified inside operating activities, so nothing is added. Capex is gross purchases of PP&E and intangibles. Judgement: the intangibles line (29,973) includes the Akero Therapeutics purchase, which Novo booked as an intangible-asset purchase rather than an acquisition of businesses; the annual report says 'Capital expenditure related to intangible assets was DKK 30.0 billion in 2025 compared with DKK 4.1 billion in 2024, reflecting business development activities, mainly related to the acquisition of Akero Therapeutics, Inc.' It is kept in capex as reported, since the filing gives no separate Akero amount. No 'acquisition of businesses' cash outflow in 2025 (a 1,004 settlement inflow for the prior year's acquisition is excluded).

classes.pricedAsReason: A shares are not listed and, under the Novo Nordisk Foundation's articles, cannot be divested; the filings state no conversion right into B shares. They are priced at the B share price because both classes have the same DKK 0.10 nominal value and, per the Annual Report 2025, 'in practice, A and B shares receive the same amount of dividend per share'. This is a valuation convention, not a conversion.

marketcap.notes: B shares are priced from the primary listing on Nasdaq Copenhagen (NOVO-B.CO, DKK) rather than the NYSE ADR (NVO, 1 ADR = 1 B share). B shares = 4,465,000,000 total A and B shares − 1,074,872,000 A shares − 58,755,131 treasury B shares = 3,331,372,869 at November 20, 2026, from Novo Nordisk's weekly buyback announcement filed on Form 6-K on November 23, 2026 (which states the total and the treasury holding but not the B count) and the 20-F cover's A-share count. Novo has been buying back B shares under a programme of up to DKK 15 billion running from February 4, 2026, so the 20-F count (3,390,128,000 B shares including treasury) is stale. Judgment call for review: the unlisted A shares are included at the B price; leaving them out would cut the value by about a quarter.
